candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance is evaluated against the Max column, the Avg column, or both changes which numeric threshold applies to a reported measurement; the default mg/l unit governs conversion for all parameters except those explicitly noted otherwise.

candidates.exact_span: T – Total; D – Dissolved; ND – Non detect
candidates.computation_change_reason: Definitions of Total versus Dissolved affect which analytical form must be compared to limits and which monitoring form is required; the meaning of ND affects whether ND entries in the limit table are enforceable numeric thresholds, how non-detect reported results are classified, and whether missing-evidence cases are resolved as compliant limits, conditional no-data, or unresolved.

A second Cyanide, T row appears later in the same table with substantially different Max/Avg values; interpreting which row applies—or whether both apply under different conditions—changes the enforceable limit used for cyanide compliance comparison.
This duplicate Cyanide, T entry conflicts with the earlier cyanide row at 0.00628/0.002854; selecting one row over the other changes the applicable Max and Avg limits by orders of magnitude.

ND appears in both Max and Avg columns; depending on whether ND is treated as a numeric detection-limit threshold or as absence of a stated limit, compliance comparison and missing-evidence classification for beryllium (and similarly marked parameters) change.
Mercury is explicitly denominated in ug/L while the table default is mg/l unless noted; misinterpreting the unit would change the applicable numeric limit by three orders of magnitude.

Phenols lacks a T or D qualifier unlike most neighboring metals; interpreting whether total, dissolved, or unspecified phenols monitoring and limits apply changes both the enforceable limit comparison and the monitoring form obligation.

TRC is not expanded or qualified in this segment; different readings of what parameter TRC denotes (and whether it is total or another form) change which reported measurements are compared and what monitoring is required.

This row states paired Max and Avg limits for Copper, T; if only one limit type is operative for compliance, choosing Max versus Avg changes whether a given reported copper value exceeds the applicable threshold.
